Priya Raghunathan spent four years maintaining the shift-scheduling system at Bracken & Doyle.

The company approved a full rewrite of the shift-scheduling system in 2021, budgeted at eighteen months.
The rewrite was cancelled after fourteen months with roughly $2 million spent and nothing shipped to production.
The old system's real specification lived in a decade of accumulated fixes that no document recorded.
Priya's team shipped 41 releases over the fourteen-month period.

The Kestrel Fen Trust completed its ninth annual transect survey of Thornlee Marsh between 12 and 19 May 2026.
Eleven transects were walked, the same eleven as in every year since 2018.
We logged 214 breeding pairs of reed bunting across the eleven transects.
We recorded four occupied territories with confidence and think there may be a fifth on the northern edge.
Water levels averaged 41 cm across the season.
The exact ten-year mean is being recomputed after we found a stuck logger at station 3, so the 62 cm we published last year should be treated as provisional.
A volunteer reported an otter with two cubs at the eastern sluice on 14 May.
We have no photograph, no spraint from that stretch, and the Trust's camera trap was offline that week.
If it is right it would be the first otter breeding record for Thornlee since 2011.
We expect to publish the full survey report in September, assuming the logger data can be recovered.
